sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAJENDRA SINGH  ON THE 10th OF MARCH, 2025
MISC. APPEAL No. 1984 of 2021  SANTOSH  Versus  SIKANDAR AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain - Advocate for the respondent

ORDER In an appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 the award dated 28.11.2022 passed in MACC No.76/2017 by First Additional Member, M.A.C.T.,Sardarpur, District - Dhar was enhanced assessing the permanent physical disability of the appellant as 100% vide order dated 04.03.2023.
2.

Vide order dated 19.09.2024 in Review Petition No.383/2024 the order dated 14.03.2023 passed in MA No.1984/2021 was recalled to the limited extend of consideration as to whether the appellant would be entitled to 25% further future prospect of rise in monthly income as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 SC.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other findings recorded in the order was kept intact and MA No.1984/2021 was restored to it's original number for hearing on the merits to the extend indicated above.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7228 2 MA-1984-2021 Heard and perused the record.
3. Tribunal has assessed the per month income of the claimant Santosh as Rs.7,000/- per month treating him only skilled labourer as he was earning livelihood from agricultural work.
His age was assessed 42 years in para 23 of the award.
In appeal his permanent physical disability was re-
assessed and treated him 100% disable instead of 25% as assessed by Tribunal but did not considered the future prospect whereas the same was raised in appeal as mentioned in para 03 of the award.

4. In National Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157 , it is held in para 61(iv) as below:-
Santosh vs Sikandar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157810994/
1 "61(iv)

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Santosh vs Sikandar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
5. Accordingly, claimant/appellant was entitled for 25% addition in the income of Rs.7,000/- per month as assessed by the Tribunal.

Therefore, head 1& 2 of para 14 of the award dated 04.03.2024 requires modification and on re-calculation the loss of future income as assessed as 8,750 x 12 x 14 =
14,70,000/- and accordingly, an amount of Rs.2,94,000/- is enhanced in the head of loss of future income and Rs.10,500/- is further enhanced in loss of income during treatment.
Hence, the appeal is allowed and the award dated 04.03.2024 is modified and a total compensation of Rs.3,04,500/- is further enhanced.
The enhanced amount shall bear the interest at the same rate as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7228 3 MA-1984-2021 awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
With the aforesaid, this misc. appeal is disposed off.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE akanksha Santosh vs Sikandar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157810994/
